To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
student teachers' performance is related to their social capital, which includes their closeness, trust and efficacy.

student teachers who are more closely connected with their peers and who trust their peers are more likely to have higher levels of self-efficacy and to achieve higher levels of performance on a high-stakes teaching performance assessment.
the social capital of the student teachers, in terms of closeness and trust, is positively associated with their performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of social relations in the learning process.
the social side of teacher learning.
how social capital and teacher efficacy are associated with performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more the pre service teachers are embedded in social relations, the more they trust and collaborate with each other, the better they perform as teachers.
social relations and social capital are important for the student teachers' performance in a high stake situation.
the social side of the teacher profession is a crucial factor in the development of teacher capabilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the student teachers' social capital is an essential factor in their performance and professional development.
social relations and social networks contribute positively to student teachers' professional development.
social capital and social relations contribute to pre service teachers' professional performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

social capital is an important resource for pre-service teachers to draw on in order to perform well in high-stakes teaching performance assessments, which is a crucial part of their teacher education.
the social capital that pre service teachers develop during their preparation is important for their learning and performance.
the social side of student teaching is an important factor to consider when preparing teachers for the profession.
